## Source scope

The employee validation driver in `apps/database/scripts` binds the current
employee creation, finalization, and restoration migration names to five rollback
test packets. Their expected counts are 25, 20, 34, 52, and 41, totaling 172
authored expectations. The original 169-expectation registration remains a
separate historical input. A source count is not PostgreSQL execution evidence.

The driver checks exact source membership and hashes, packet order, and strict
TAP plans. It rejects old migration names, the old finalization count of 31,
failed or skipped assertions, TODOs, bailouts, duplicate plans, truncated output,
and packets without their closing rollback. The TypeScript contract file remains
uncompiled until genuine generated schema and installed dependencies are admitted.

## Default denied entry

The dedicated entry requires exact reviewed admission and a native supervisor
with an authenticated clock and transport. That native backend is unimplemented.
Missing arguments, malformed admission, and absent native supervision deny entry.
`runtimeAdmission` remains `null` and DENIED. Execution, provider, readiness, and
activation flags remain OFF. Injected success callbacks and broker capacity do
not establish physical admission.

Existing shared Supabase lifecycle and type generation APIs retain their behavior.
The staging helper accepts an optional partial-root removal callback and
diagnostic callback. Default removal still removes its guarded partial root.
A dedicated caller can retain that root for recovery. A cleanup failure emits
a secondary diagnostic while the original staging error remains primary.
Retention alone does not prove a durable acknowledgement or closed resources.

## Finite source verification

`employee-validation-source-contract.test.mjs` checks the current source names,
count map, TAP text contracts, and default denial. It uses pure rejection fixtures
and does not execute the successful source verification or admission path.
`employee-validation-stage-cleanup.test.mjs` calls the actual staging helper with
an explicit synthetic file list and new temporary fixture roots. It checks
default removal, custom retention, and double-failure precedence before any
configuration rewrite or metadata creation. Each fixture is bounded to 4096
bytes, two files, and twelve directories and removes only its own fresh root.

The root `bun test:scripts` runner explicitly registers these two source tests.
Use `node scripts/run-script-tests.js --list` to inspect membership without
executing tests. After the ordinary script batch succeeds, the runner executes
only this pair in one Node process with test isolation disabled, concurrency one,
a 64 MiB V8 old-space limit, and a 60-second process deadline enforced with
SIGKILL. A failure or unknown exit stops the run. The old-space limit does not
cap total process memory. Four previously registered database tests remain in the
ordinary batch; this change adds no other database scripts or runtime gates.
This registration provides no SQL, Auth, provider, or physical admission evidence.

Run selected source tests through the existing resource broker from the owning
checkout, with one Node process and worker, a 64 MiB heap, and a deadline of at
most 60 seconds. Import-binding checks after relocation remain source evidence.
Do not substitute these tests for SQL, type generation, Auth, or customer proof.

## Physical admission remains held

A separately authorized host-owned unit must supply the actual dedicated
machine and boot identity, canonical checkout and roots, exclusive daemon
identity, authenticated supervisor, immutable installed binaries and image
closure, and exact source and effective configuration identities. It must
establish provider, mail, and hook denial and approved ordinary GoTrue behavior.
The baseline repository configuration does not establish those properties.

Physical containment must cover all producers and descendants before first
CREATE. It needs aggregate CPU, memory, process, disk-byte and inode quotas,
bounded logs, one OS deadline, controller-loss sealing, and independent recovery.
Policy remains 4 CPUs, 8 GiB memory, zero extra swap, 1024 PIDs, 16 GiB disk,
256 MiB logs, a 900-second maximum, and at least 60 seconds reserved for closure.
Source policy constants and cooperative timers do not enforce those limits.

Independent closure evidence must cover PostgreSQL sessions, HTTP outcomes,
descendants, daemon resources, retained roots, and the final control ledger.
Unknown outcomes retain recovery material and cannot authorize retry or adoption.
Protected hosts and PKTM remain excluded.

The complete current SQL packets, installed compiler and genuine generated
types, ordinary GoTrue creation and deferred checks, C1/C2 service cast removal,
C3 Mail compatibility, employee creation/restoration/reload/privacy behavior,
and customer or production delivery remain separate unfinished gates. This page
provides no admission, credential acquisition, bootstrap, or execution recipe.
